# T002 — Backend HTTP and ACS contract characterization

## Summary
Added 12 backend characterization cases (15 total with T001's three DTMF normalization cases) against unchanged production code. All service boundaries use offline fakes; no Azure client or credential is used.

## Changes (files and why)
- `backend/tests/server.characterization.test.js`: seven cases exercise the real Express routes in an isolated child process: `/health` JSON/connectivity, missing fields and permissive omitted amount/merchant/currency, initiation response and serialized transaction/audit, failed initiation, missing and legacy status, hangup and callback response, connected/approval/disconnect transitions, rejected/escalated tone aliases, retry and timeout events.
- `backend/tests/fixtures/offline-server.js`: hooks call, TTS, storage and dotenv dependencies before importing the real server. Its offline call adapter additionally checks the complete forwarded initiation request for both omitted defaults and legacy merchant alias/currency. Child environment contains only port, locale, timezone and PATH.
- `backend/tests/call-service.characterization.test.js`: three cases pin en-US verification and confirmation speech, E.164 check, synthesized audio/storage inputs, ACS client constructor, invitation, callback URI and options, status lookup and `hangUp(true)`.
- `backend/tests/webhook-media.characterization.test.js`: two cases pin stored-audio fallback, media cancellation/playback, DTMF recognition options/context, unsupported `Tone3` prompt and recognition retry. No production, manifests, or lockfiles changed.

## Decisions (rationale and sources)
- The approved plan T002 calls for offline route, webhook and ACS adapter characterization before dependencies change; the assessed baseline has no live test services. Node's synchronous module load hooks intercept SDK and service imports so assertions execute unchanged application code without placing calls.
- Preserve observed quirks rather than correcting them: `/health` reports healthy despite offline ACS; initiation lists amount, merchant and currency as required but accepts them omitted; a failed call stays queryable; disconnect retains approved status; callbacks for unknown transactions return plain-text `OK`. These follow `backend/server.js`, `backend/services/call-service.js` and `backend/services/webhook-handler.js`.

## Validation (commands and results)
- From root with `CI=true TZ=UTC LANG=C.UTF-8`: `npm ci` — pass; `npm run build --if-present` — pass (existing CSS optimizer warnings); `npm test` — 15 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped; `npm run lint --if-present` — pass (existing warnings).
- Compared with T001's three passing tests: 12 additional tests, no reduced discovery or new failures. These checks run on Node 22 as approved for T001–T003; Node 24 validation belongs to T004.

## Follow-ups and risks
- The Express child uses a temporary loopback port; all cloud-facing modules are replaced by in-process fakes. Do not treat the suite as a live ACS integration test.
- Existing CSS optimizer/lint warnings remain; do not suppress or conflate them with this test-only task.
